center.title: The last page earns it
center.detail: Elizabeth, with no power and no debt left to collect, asks the man whose control cost a life to come along, and the reader believes both her question and his “No.”
center.thesis: Control is not competence. When you treat future possibility as leverage, you eventually destroy your ability to choose, and other people pay for your convenience.
center.test: If a character says the theme out loud, it's failed.

pillars.title: Elizabeth chooses her way here
pillars.why: The invitation only means something if she has been choosing, one rung at a time, all book.

cells.label: Opens the chained door
cells.quote: She turned the lock and opened it against the chain.
cells.note: First small independent act, before any magic (R50).

cells.label: Grabs the cookbook back
cells.quote: Elizabeth grabbed the cookbook by the spine and pulled it from his hands.
cells.note: Property defense under pressure (R49).

cells.label: Goes after her books
cells.note: She follows for the cookbook, not for him. Constrained, not consent (Q118).

cells.label: Chooses the forest over the sidewalk
cells.quote: She had put them there herself, after the shopkeeper had offered to send her back to the sidewalk.
cells.note: The first choice made with her books back (R31).

cells.label: Cuts him out of the blob
cells.quote: Elizabeth already had the dagger in her hand.
cells.note: Stansbury made the tool; she chose to use it (Q106).

cells.label: Puts the car in the ditch
cells.note: The midpoint crash, chosen (Non-Negotiable 4).

cells.label: Refuses rescue
cells.quote: I don't need to be rescued.
cells.note: He overrides her anyway; the museum pays (Non-Negotiable 6).

cells.label: Runs to Milo
cells.note: No spell, dagger unused, diary and cookbook passed by (R45).

pillars.title: Pathwell decides for people
pillars.why: The controlling idea made flesh. Each step is help nobody asked for, until the last step is help he withholds.

cells.label: The invented certainty
cells.quote: Your house has now been marked, magically speaking.
cells.note: Half-bluff over a real, misread danger (Ledger P4, transformed).

cells.label: A choice while holding her things
cells.note: Blind-spot irony, locked (Q118); inverted in Ch18 (Ledger R4).

cells.label: Buys what nobody ordered
cells.quote: Did Camp Cunnan ask you for all of this?
cells.note: Pays with his own future and clears the old debt (Non-Negotiable 1).

cells.label: The self-appointed delivery
cells.note: Camp needed it and didn't ask (Ledger R8).

cells.label: The Ask
cells.note: Morally paid. What the original problem was stays open by lock (Q141).

cells.label: Overrides her at the museum
cells.quote: She wasn't yours to take from.
cells.note: Shade says it; the discharge destroys the records and hurts her.

cells.label: Builds the frame over a no
cells.note: Shade refuses, Mama Baga says stop, he forces it (Non-Negotiable 7).

cells.label: Doesn't call for help
cells.quote: He was close enough to hear Shade calling.
cells.note: Shown, not explained; he confesses it in Ch18 (R46).

pillars.title: Pathwell reckons, without a pardon
pillars.why: So the invitation reads as her choice, not his absolution.

cells.label: Sees the torn page
cells.note: The first time he registers a cost to her.

cells.label: The mirror turns toward him
cells.quote: Something points in an unpleasant direction,
cells.note: “Mine.” The mystery starts pointing at him.

cells.label: Mama Baga says stop
cells.note: He doesn't. That's the point (Q145).

cells.label: Restitution, defined by Camp
cells.note: Evidence, not absolution (Q133, Q143).

cells.label: Elizabeth refuses to make it mean something
cells.quote: I am not going to make your guilt useful.
cells.note: Her line, not the narrator's.

cells.label: Asks first, takes the no
cells.note: “And the wagon remains yellow.”

cells.label: Puts the other cookbook back
cells.quote: put it back on the end of the shelf where it had been, square to the edge.
cells.note: Silent; he doesn't find out if he can still prune (Q96, Q99, Q103).

cells.label: Confesses
cells.note: From shame, before her comparison; he refuses the equivalence (Version C).

pillars.title: Shade is a person
pillars.why: His death has to cost something, or Pathwell's omission costs nothing.

cells.label: The wrong reflection
cells.quote: like hearing your own voice on a recording and recognizing every word without recognizing the man who said them.
cells.note: Before anyone knows he exists.

cells.label: He names himself
cells.note: Roadside reveal kept over the August lock; W16 is still with the author.

cells.label: Doesn't confess for Pathwell
cells.quote: He knows what he did. Ask him.
cells.note: Shade's restraint makes the Ask hers (Non-Negotiable 5).

cells.label: Bad at Hearts
cells.note: Personhood in small things: coffee, the green jacket, pockets.

cells.label: Wants something
cells.note: His own want, not Pathwell's problem.

cells.label: Says no
cells.note: The refusal a blind reader called the strongest dialogue in the book.

cells.label: Fights to live
cells.note: Caught while helping; no consent, no serene acceptance (R46).

cells.label: Camp names him
cells.note: “LIKED POCKETS.”

pillars.title: Her records are given, not taken
pillars.why: What he took in Ch1 she gives away herself by Ch12, and loses by choice in Ch15.

cells.label: Nana's ink lights up
cells.quote: Gold ran along the ink in little starts and stops
cells.note: The magic belongs to the person who wrote the page (R51).

cells.label: The page tears
cells.quote: The sugar-cookie page stayed under his palm.
cells.note: The tear itself isn't shown yet. EXP-0015 B3 / C3 waiting.

cells.label: Nana's name for her
cells.note: The echo sends her after the cookbook (R21).

cells.label: Returned by the shop, not by him
cells.quote: These were never his to spend.
cells.note: The rebuke the P65 reader liked best.

cells.label: Given whole
cells.note: One page spent healing a stranger (Non-Negotiable 3).

cells.label: The diary donated
cells.quote: Ask me before anyone reads it.
cells.note: Ownership passes to the archive (Ledger O3).

cells.label: She runs past both
cells.note: Rhymes with Ch4's “That was the choice.” (Ledger R6).

cells.label: The sugar cookies come back
cells.note: One line in a list. The cold reader wanted more; any return is the author's line (Ledger O2).

pillars.title: Camp is help that asks
pillars.why: The other way to help, so the reader can see what Pathwell's way costs without anyone saying it.

cells.label: Asks her, not him
cells.note: He answers for her; she answers for herself: “Less than I was.”

cells.label: Welcomes her
cells.note: Clothes, the gold chain, the tucked hair (R41).

cells.label: The archive
cells.note: Records kept for people who still need them.

cells.label: Milo's sock
cells.quote: One sock had surrendered halfway down his calf.
cells.note: Runs to the fire and after (Ledger R11).

cells.label: Why she picks Camp
cells.quote: Mama Baga didn't ask me anything I didn't want to tell her.
cells.note: Chosen because nobody controls the room there.

cells.label: The blue notebook saved
cells.quote: Stansbury came back out through the side window carrying the blue road notebook
cells.note: Camp's own record survives (Ledger O8).

cells.label: Pathwell carries boxes where told
cells.note: Restraint shown in one gesture.

cells.label: Clean hands, one section
cells.quote: clean hands, a pencil, and exactly one section
cells.note: “Copy the smudge.”

pillars.title: The mysteries play fair
pillars.why: The reader has to trust the withholding. Every held question gets a hand-off or a payoff.

cells.label: At the door before any magic
cells.quote: Something wet and dark sagged into the gap.
cells.note: The clue that the blob isn't hers (Ledger P3).

cells.label: A true line said as a joke
cells.note: Literally what the creature is.

cells.label: Why was he in her apartment?
cells.note: Nobody asks, all book. Author's fix: “What are you still doing here?” (EXP-0015 B0) paired with her Ch3 inference (B1).

cells.label: How much future is left?
cells.note: Open by ruling: he chooses not to find out (Q96, R19).

cells.label: It came first; then it ate the waste
cells.note: “The first part did not.” The question becomes hers.

cells.label: It goes for him
cells.note: “No.” Pathwell corrects his own misread.

cells.label: Never the point
cells.quote: Then you were never the point.
cells.note: The target misdirection paid (Ledger P3, P4).

cells.label: The draw goes quiet
cells.note: Because the anomaly is gone, not because of a mechanic (Ledger P8).

pillars.title: The bookend turns over
pillars.why: The first page's exchange comes back with the roles swapped, and the small ordinary things carry it.

cells.label: He asks; she says no
cells.note: Momentum over her. “Perfect.” is his.

cells.label: The first line
cells.quote: It was the crash that woke her.
cells.note: Boxes falling, not the blob (R27).

cells.label: Perfectly crappy
cells.note: The book's taste for honest, ordinary things starts here.

cells.label: Terrible coffee
cells.note: Recurs through Ch9, 10, 13, 16, 18 (Ledger R7).

cells.label: The first line, chosen
cells.quote: It was the crash that woke her.
cells.note: Bare, at the midpoint (R11).

cells.label: The spoon
cells.note: Ordinary life stays aggressively itself.

cells.label: She asks to go
cells.quote: You asked me to take you somewhere.
cells.note: He checks whether anything was actually requested.

cells.label: She asks; he says no
cells.note: “Perfect.” is hers now (R9).

loose.text: Ch2's changed neighborhood: displacement or magic?
Ch8 roadside reveal and Ch11 museum staging kept over August locks
The nine o'clock meeting: set up five times, paid lightly
“Leo” and “big cat”: used once, in Ch10
Ch4: why the healer can't use the cart's records (test with readers)
